claims.statement: For each fixed independence number a, every ordinary tree T with alpha(T)=a has order at most 2a and hence lies in a finite isomorphism-class search domain; furthermore, all original leaves sharing an original support have identical Delta_p(T-v) selector values and identical selected summands, so their full tagged contribution is exactly their multiplicity times the common summand.
claims.scope: Exact fixed-a finite reduction and same-support compression for finite ordinary trees, preserving the strict selector and tagged aggregate. This provides no uniform bound over a and no sign conclusion for the complete sum.
claims.reason: Bipartition classes are independent, giving |V(T)|<=2a. Swapping any two leaves with the same support is a tree automorphism, which preserves T-v up to isomorphism, maps T-{v,s_v} to the corresponding deletion for the other leaf, and leaves T-N[s_v] unchanged. Multiplicity therefore reproduces exactly the original selected-tag sum. The argument is elementary and complete for its stated scope, but parameterwise finiteness does not resolve the unbounded-a assertion or control compensation between supports.

limitations: The finite enumeration bound depends on a=alpha(T), which is unbounded in the primary target.
No global sign bound follows from support-profile compression; positive contributions may be offset elsewhere.
No exhaustive computation, witness, imported theorem, or resolution of the primary target is claimed.
